messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — automated SLO monitor detected elevated latency for /v1/generate (us-west-2). p95 jumped from ~480ms to ~2.1s, p99 from ~1.1s to ~6.7s over last 5m. Error rate nominal. Auto-page to oncall.

Elaine (oncall): Oncall Elaine here — joining triage. Thanks bot. What is the scope? Customers impacted, streaming or non-streaming?

Mike (runtime): Seeing big increase in queue depth at the tokenizer/preproc tier. Tokenizer CPU on tokr-pool saturated, per-host CPU ~98%. Many long-running jobs in streaming sessions (idle waiting while ingesting).

Samir (preproc): Confirmed. Index of delays points to prompt-template expansion + JSON-mode validation step taking ~300–800ms extra per request for certain tool-schema payloads. Affected requests often contain large tool schemas and nested arrays.

Rachel (infra): infra telemetry: autoscaler hasn't spun up extra tokenizer workers yet due to cooldown + pod density limits in the cluster. We have two nodes at 100% and one node with 30% reserve.

Elaine (oncall): OK: immediate mitigation suggestions? Can we short-circuit JSON-mode for top-impacted routes, or throttle heavy customers?

Mike (runtime): Two low-friction mitigations: 1) toggle `preproc.json_mode=false` at the route level for the streaming route for 10 minutes, 2) enable emergency-burst nodes in the dedicated pool (if quota allows).

Samir (preproc): I can push a quick runtime patch that disables deep schema validation for requests > 2k chars (heuristic). Patch is small but needs a quick deploy. Alternatively we can flip the control-plane flag to bypass JSON-mode for specific project ids.

Jess (cs): We've already got one enterprise customer messaging support complaining about slow responses. CS wants a short note we can send that says we're mitigating and will follow-up.

Rachel (infra): I can unfreeze the autoscaler and trigger two spare tokenizer nodes from the reserve. ETA for nodes to be ready ~3–4 minutes. If we need capacity faster, we can route new requests to us-east-1 (but cross-region adds latency for those customers).

Elaine (oncall): Actions: Mike -> toggle route-level json_mode bypass; Rachel -> spin up nodes; Samir -> prepare fast patch; Jess -> draft CS blurb. I'll coordinate and then hand off to next oncall if this persists.

Mike (runtime): Executing route toggle now via control plane. Command: 
```bash
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routes/toggle" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","project_scope":"streaming","preproc":{"json_mode":false}}'
```
Response: 200 OK. Patch applied to 3 routing hosts.

ops-bot: Deploy log: route-toggle job 86912 completed by Mike at 2701112235.

Samir (preproc): Kicked off a debug run against a sampled set of heavy payloads. Initial profiler shows JSON schema validation in preproc call stack is hot: `SchemaValidator::validateRecursive` (median 450ms per call for worst cases). Also notable: repeated re-parsing of prompt templates when requests include dynamic tool schema fragments.

Mike (runtime): After toggle, seeing immediate drop in p95 in the next 60s — p95 down to ~610ms, p99 ~1.6s. Still above SLO but much improved. Queue depth on tokenizer nodes dropping.

Rachel (infra): New tokenizer nodes are booting. One is ready; second approx +90s. Observed pod evictions queued on older nodes as new nodes accept traffic.

Elaine (oncall): Good. Jess — suggested customer message: "We're aware of intermittent slowness affecting streaming generation for some requests. We've deployed an emergency mitigation and are scaling capacity. No data loss. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline." Can you send?

Jess (cs): Sent to affected contacts. Will post copy in the incident Jira.

Samir (preproc): While mitigation buys us time, root cause summary so far: heavy requests with large nested tool schemas cause expensive validation + template hydration. Two compounding issues: 1) JSON-mode validation is synchronous and re-entrant per tool fragment, 2) prompt-template rendering currently reparses schema tokens on every request instead of caching compiled templates for schema variants.

Mike (runtime): I pushed a short-lived cache in the runtime that caches compiled template AST keyed by schema fingerprint. Rolling out to 20% canary now. If stable, we can ramp.

ops-bot: Canary rollout started by Mike at 2701112304 -> hosts: tokr-canary-{01..04}. Monitor p95/p99.

Elaine (oncall): Monitoring: keep an eye on p99 tail. We care if streaming stalls reappear. Also track customer error traces for `stalling-during-tokenize`.

Samir (preproc): I have a dev patch ready to short-circuit deep validation when route has `json_mode: bypassed` and to add schema-fingerprint caching. Will submit for fast review. Estimated QA + rollout 25–30m if we do full CI.

Rachel (infra): All requested nodes are live. Aggregate tokenizer capacity up ~60%. No quota limits hit.

Mike (runtime): Canary metrics: p95 on canary hosts ~430ms, p99 ~900ms — significantly better than baseline. I'll promote to 50% if no regression in 5m.

Elaine (oncall): Hand-off plan: I'll stick on triage for next 20m. If metrics hold and canary is promoted, we can move to recovery state and let engineering owners finish the long-fix. If p99 spikes again, re-page the oncall rotation.

Jess (cs): Notified key customers and updated status page: "Mitigation in place; partial service degradation has been reduced. Engineers are triaging."

Samir (preproc): Posting quick repro and stack snapshot to the incident ticket for postmortem: 
```json
{
  "request_id": "r-3f9a8c2",
  "payload_size": 18240,
  "tool_schema_count": 12,
  "median_schema_fragment_size": 614
}
```
This triggers the expensive validation path.

Mike (runtime): Promoted canary to 50% at 2701112360. Monitoring window started. No errors.

ops-bot: Metric update: p95=490ms, p99=1.1s (rolling 5m) at 2701112400.

Elaine (oncall): Recovery notes for timeline: mitigation (route json_mode bypass) applied by Mike at 2701112235; autoscaler and nodes added by Rachel by 2701112278; canary cache rollout started 2701112304 -> promoted 2701112360. p95/p99 improved but still above SLO for some tail cases.

Jess (cs): Customers acknowledged the update and appreciate the transparency. Logged impacted tenant list to the incident ticket.

Samir (preproc): Next steps for long-term: 1) implement schema-fingerprint caching + compiled template cache, 2) make JSON-mode validation async or incremental, 3) add guards to reject/queue extremely large tool schemas or move heavy validation to background lane. I'll open tickets and assign owners.

Elaine (oncall): Handing off to next oncall (Tom) at 2701112480 if everything stable. Tom — brief: temporary bypass toggled, extra nodes up, canary cache promoted to 50%, long fix owned by Samir. Watch p99 tail and any regression in streaming stalls.

ops-bot: Hand-off recorded at 2701112480. Incident severity reduced to SEV3; follow-up postmortem requested.
